b: Frankfort, Ky. — Governor Andy Beshear signed an executive order creating the Kentucky Office of Outdoor Recreation, making Kentucky the 26th state in the nation to stand up a dedicated office to grow its outdoor recreation economy. Outdoor Recreation Roundtable (ORR), a coalition of associations and organizations across the outdoor recreation economy, applauded the Governor’s action and welcomed Seth Wheat as the Office’s inaugural Executive Director.

In the announcement, Kentucky shared that Governor Beshear signed an executive order creating the Kentucky Office of Outdoor Recreation and directing it to sustain, manage and grow the Commonwealth’s outdoor recreation industry through promotion, education, community resources and support for outdoor recreation development. The office will also oversee the Kentucky Trail Town program, a tourism and economic development initiative designed to provide communities with a strategic plan to capitalize on recreational opportunities. The program currently has 32 participating communities that have publicly committed to sharing their outdoor opportunities, culture, history and stories with guests.

“Governor Beshear’s announcement of the Kentucky Office of Outdoor Recreation is a smart investment in Kentucky’s economic future, public health, and quality of life,” said Whitney Potter Schwartz, Interim President of the Outdoor Recreation Roundtable (ORR). “From the mountains of eastern Kentucky to the lakes and rivers out west, from the bluegrass hills of horse country to the Daniel Boone National Forest, the Commonwealth’s great outdoors are among its greatest competitive advantages. A dedicated Office of Outdoor Recreation will help Kentucky protect and promote those places, support the small businesses and communities that depend on them, and expand access to time outside, which research shows improves mental and physical health, strengthens communities, and lowers the overall cost of care. ORR looks forward to working with Executive Director Seth Wheat as he takes on this important role, and to helping Kentucky realize the full promise of its outdoor recreation economy.”

“Our record-breaking $14.6 billion tourism industry is essential to our commonwealth’s success and outdoor recreation is a major driver that this industry and our local communities depend on,” said Gov. Beshear. “The new Office of Outdoor Recreation will expand on opportunities from east to west and north to south to attract more visitors to our New Kentucky Home and further support jobs, local businesses and communities across our commonwealth.”

“This office will help connect communities with the resources and support they need to develop outdoor recreation experiences and create new economic opportunities,” said Tourism, Arts and Heritage Cabinet Secretary Lindy Casebier. “We appreciate Gov. Beshear’s continued investment in Kentucky’s tourism industry, making the commonwealth a premier place to visit, work and live.”

“This is an exciting day for the commonwealth. Outdoor recreation positively impacts so many aspects of life here in Kentucky, and I am eager to help grow this important industry,” said Seth Wheat, Executive Director of the Kentucky Office of Outdoor Recreation. “With the Governor’s announcement today, Kentucky is showing its commitment as a place that values outdoor recreation for all the positive economic, physical and cultural benefits it brings.”

New data released this year by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Economic Analysis Outdoor Recreation Satellite Account (ORSA) shows that in 2025, outdoor recreation generated $6.6 billion in GDP for Kentucky — 2.1% of the state’s economy — and supported 58,359 Kentucky jobs. The largest outdoor recreation activities in the Commonwealth by economic impact include boating and fishing; hunting, shooting and trapping; equestrian; RVing; and climbing, hiking and tent camping.

Nationally, outdoor recreation is a $1.3 trillion economic powerhouse — 2.3% of U.S. GDP — supporting 5.3 million jobs. The outdoor recreation economy has grown 45.3% in real terms since 2012, outpacing the broader U.S. economy and underscoring the sector’s role as one of the country’s most consistent engines of job creation and small business growth, particularly in rural communities.

“From mountain to river, wilderness to city, Kentucky recognizes the value of outdoor recreation as a driver of prosperity, health, and quality of life,” said Nathan Reigner, Chair of the Confluence of States and Director of the Pennsylvania Office of Outdoor Recreation. “On behalf of our 23-state bipartisan coalition, we congratulate Kentucky and welcome the Commonwealth to our national movement growing and strengthening state-level outdoor economies.”

The Outdoor Recreation Roundtable is a coalition of outdoor recreation associations representing more than 110,000 outdoor businesses in the recreation economy and the full spectrum of outdoor-related activities. The most recent data from the U.S. Department of Commerce shows that outdoor recreation generated $1.3 trillion in economic output (2.3% of GDP) and accounts for 5.3 million jobs.
